senses.gloss:
1. वृंह् वृंह्, बृंह् बृंह्, i. 1, Par.
 1. To grow, to increase.
 2. To roar, Śiś. 17, 31 (Ātm.).
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. वृंहित.
 1. Increased.
 2. Cerished, MBh. 2, 2589.
 3. Nourished. n. The roar of elephants, Kir. 7, 39.
 --Caus. To augment, MBh. 3, 11334.
 --With the prep. उप उप, Caus. To augment, Dev. 8, 8. उपवृंहित,
 1. Collected from.
 2. Possessed of, endowed with, Daśak. in Chr. 182, 6.
 --With समुप सम्-उप, To augment, MBh. 1, 260.
 --Cf. वृह्; βράχω, βράζω, βράγχος, βρόγχος, βρόχθος, probably also βράσσω, and βρυχάομαι; ῥόχθος, ὀρεχθέω, ῥαχία, ῥέγχω, ῥόγχος, and probably ῥύγχος, ῥυζέω.
† 2. वृंह् वृंह्, बृंह् बृंह्, i. 10, Par. To speak, to shine.

वृंहण वृंहण, i. e. 1. वृंह् + अन,
 I. adj. Nourishing.
 II. m. A kind of sweetmeat.

वृन्त वृन्त, n.
 1. The nipple.
 2. The foot, stalk of a leaf or fruit, Mālat. 16, 20.
 3. The stand of a water-jar.
 --Comp.
वृन्तिका वृन्तिका, i. e. वृन्त + क, f. A small stalk, MBh. 1, 1443.

वृन्द वृन्द,
 I. adj. Many, all.
 II. n.
 1. A heap, Chr. 25, 62.
 2. A multitude, Pañc. 222, 23; Bhartṛ. 3, 47.
 III. f. दा, Holy basil, Ocymum sanctum.
 --Comp.

वृन्दार वृन्दार, i. e. वृन्द + आर (cf. the next), adj. Comparat. वृन्दीयंस्; superl. वृन्दिष्ठ.
 1. Eminent.
 2. Beautiful, Lass. 2. ed. 88, 20.

वृन्दारक वृन्दार + क,
 I. adj.
 1. Much, great.
 2. Excellent, chief, venerable, Bhaṭṭ. 2, 45.
 3. Handsome.
 II. m.
 1. The head of a crowd or herd.
 2. A deity.
ऽवृन्दिन् -वृन्दिन्, in अश्व-, i. e. -वृन्द + इन्, adj. Consisting in a multitude of horses, MBh. 5, 5703.
वृन्दिष्ठ वृन्दिष्ठ, वृन्दीयंस् वृन्दीयंस्, see वृन्दार.
